design.name: sync_fifo4x16
design.description: Implement a synthesizable SystemVerilog synchronous FIFO named sync_fifo4x16 with exactly four unsigned 16-bit entries and the exact declared top-level interface. All state changes occur only on rising edges of clk. rst_n is synchronous, active-low, and has highest priority. A rising edge that samples rst_n low clears the FIFO by setting all four 16-bit register-array entries, the 2-bit read pointer, 2-bit write pointer, 3-bit occupancy level, and dedicated 16-bit registered head_data to zero. The externally visible reset state is level=0, out_valid=0, out_data=16'h0000, and in_ready=1. Deasserting rst_n does not add a guard cycle: the first rising edge that samples rst_n high performs normal enqueue and dequeue transfers. Store all four FIFO entries in exactly one 4x16-bit register array addressed circularly by the pointers, synchronously clear every array entry to zero when rst_n is sampled low, and use exactly one additional 16-bit registered head_data as the stable output-head copy. Do not move all queued entries through a shift register. Define dequeue acceptance as out_valid && out_ready and enqueue acceptance as in_valid && in_ready. out_valid is one exactly when level is nonzero. out_data is head_data whenever nonempty and is zero whenever empty; there is no combinational fall-through or empty-queue bypass from in_data. in_ready is one whenever level is below four, and at level four remains one exactly when a dequeue is accepted in the same cycle. An accepted enqueue always writes in_data at the current write pointer and advances the 2-bit write pointer by natural binary wraparound without a modulo operator. An enqueue into a previously empty FIFO also loads head_data with in_data. An accepted dequeue removes the current oldest entry and advances the 2-bit read pointer by natural binary wraparound without a modulo operator. A dequeue from a prior level greater than one loads head_data from the next-oldest array entry at read_ptr plus one; a simultaneous dequeue and enqueue from a prior level of one loads head_data directly from in_data because that accepted input becomes the sole queued item; a dequeue-only operation from a prior level of one clears head_data to zero. Enqueue-only increments level, dequeue-only decrements level, simultaneous accepted enqueue and dequeue leave level unchanged while advancing both pointers, and no accepted operation preserves level and both pointers. When empty with in_valid=1 and out_ready=1, only enqueue can occur on that edge; out_valid and out_data must not expose the new input before the edge and become valid from the resulting post-edge state. When full with out_valid=1 and out_ready=1, an enqueue may be accepted on the same edge as the dequeue so sustained full-rate traffic transfers one item in each direction per cycle. While out_valid=1 and out_ready=0, out_valid, head_data, out_data, and the read pointer must remain stable; an independently accepted enqueue may update the array, write pointer, and occupancy without advancing or replacing the stalled head. Preserve strict first-in-first-out ordering through pointer wraparound and all simultaneous operations. Never overflow, underflow, lose, duplicate, or reorder accepted data. Use exactly one 4x16 register array, one 16-bit registered head_data, one 2-bit read pointer, one 2-bit write pointer, and one 3-bit occupancy counter. Do not use vendor IP, initial blocks, declaration initialization, delays, force or release, division, DPI, file I/O, system tasks, or other unsynthesizable constructs.

requirements.text: A rising edge sampling rst_n low has highest priority, clears all four 16-bit storage-array entries plus head_data, both pointers, and level to zero, and logically empties the FIFO. The visible reset state and the state before the first deasserted edge are level=0, out_valid=0, out_data=0, and in_ready=1; the first edge sampling rst_n high immediately permits normal transfer.
A rising edge accepts in_data exactly when in_valid and in_ready are both one; rejected input must not change FIFO data or the write pointer.
A rising edge removes the oldest entry exactly when out_valid and out_ready are both one; an empty FIFO cannot dequeue.
All accepted 16-bit unsigned values are returned exactly once in strict first-in-first-out order across read-pointer and write-pointer wraparound, with no loss, duplication, or reordering.
out_valid is one exactly when level is nonzero. When nonempty, out_data continuously presents the oldest queued entry; when empty, out_data is zero.
Whenever out_valid is one and out_ready is zero, out_valid and out_data remain stable until that item is accepted, and dequeue-side state does not advance during any length of backpressure.
in_ready is one whenever level is below four. At level four it is one exactly when out_valid and out_ready cause a same-cycle dequeue; otherwise it is zero.

level always remains from zero through four inclusive; enqueue-only increments it, dequeue-only decrements it, simultaneous accepted enqueue and dequeue leave it unchanged, and no accepted transfer leaves it unchanged.

When empty with in_valid=1 and out_ready=1, the current cycle cannot dequeue or combinationally expose in_data. The edge enqueues the item, and out_valid with that item appears only in the post-edge state.

When full and a dequeue succeeds, in_ready remains one so an asserted in_valid is accepted on the same edge; the previous head is removed, the new value becomes the newest tail, and level remains four.

The FIFO never overflows or underflows: full input without a successful dequeue is rejected, empty output requests remove nothing, and rejected operations cannot corrupt pointers, occupancy, or queued data.
After filling, continuous in_valid and out_ready sustain one accepted dequeue and one accepted enqueue on every rising edge while preserving order and constant occupancy.

directed_tests.description: Create nonempty state, assert synchronous reset while requests are active, then deassert reset with in_valid high to exercise immediate normal transfer on the first released edge.
Accept one patterned word, hold it for one cycle, dequeue it, and issue additional empty output requests without corrupting state.
From empty, assert in_valid and out_ready together, retain the resulting item without accepting it for a cycle, then dequeue it later.
Fill all four slots with distinct values, attempt blocked input while full, then perform full-state simultaneous dequeue/enqueue and drain the resulting queue in order.
Queue multiple distinct words, hold out_ready low for a long interval while varying input requests, and then drain in exact order.
Preload four distinct words and sustain simultaneous input and output long enough for both two-bit pointers to wrap repeatedly, then drain and verify all accepted values end to end.
Apply continuous input across empty, partial, and full states, then continuous output through nonempty and empty states.

assumptions: Inputs are sampled immediately before each rising edge and outputs are checked after post-edge combinational settling.
Because reset is synchronous, rst_n becoming low does not change state until a rising edge samples it low; the required reset outputs are observed after that edge.
The first rising edge sampling rst_n high after reset deassertion performs normal enqueue and dequeue logic without an extra guard cycle.
Each rising edge sampling rst_n low synchronously resets all four 16-bit storage-array entries and the registered head_data to zero in addition to resetting both pointers and level.

The dedicated registered head_data is a copy of the oldest queued array entry, is loaded directly on an enqueue into empty, is advanced on a successful dequeue when data remains, and is never modified by an independent enqueue into a nonempty FIFO.
All input combinations within the declared unsigned widths are legal, and in_data is semantically ignored unless enqueue is accepted.
